performance.rootCause: Interpreted native 64-round SHA-256 and per-row source joins ran across the whole owner feed before the count facet, making cost depend on population rather than page size.
performance.selectedOptimization: Native Node SHA-256 with bounded request-local minimal tuples; batch-owned Job/Application source validation; simple MongoDB exact rows/count facet restricted to fully validated IDs; hydrate names/titles only for returned page. No per-row network queries.
integrityGuarantees: Canonical digest uses the existing lifecycle application key generator, exposed as an internal helper; no alternative identity or marker.

Original job/applicant/organization/recruiter tuple, consent version/date/boolean and supported lifecycle status are checked before totals. Exact BSON scalar type guards exclude malformed array-shaped values.
No private names, notes, PDF bytes or portfolio evidence are needed in the integrity scan/source maps.
Owner/org/membership/settings authority, all reads and final page access fences remain in the accepted snapshot transaction. No cross-request identity/authorization cache.
Forged hashes, source mismatches, malformed consent and changed owners cannot influence successful totals. No schema, marker, backfill, dependency, production index or migration introduced.
performance.budgetAndCapacity: Shared five-second validation/query budget retained. Stream batches of 256, maximum 10,000 provisional identity rows and bounded source maps. Exceeding capacity or deadline returns explicit 503, never a successful truncated total.
performance.memory: Actual Node RSS/heap before/after and sample peaks are retained in each benchmark report. Optimized sequential sampled heap peaks were ~64.9 MiB (261) and ~60.1 MiB (1000), including the fixture, driver and other loaded services, not isolated per-request allocations. Mongo fixture cache configured at 0.25 GiB; sort sizes/spills retained in explain.
limitations: Seven sequential measured requests after warmup and two waves of three reads are local evidence, not production capacity or an SLA.

All seven 1000-record baseline sequential requests timed out; their p50/p95 describe time-to-failure, not successful response latency. Optimized sequential/simultaneous/mixed requests had zero failures/timeouts.
Exact validation remains O(owner population) within the explicit 10,000-row capacity. Larger pools need a separately reviewed design; no silent truncation.
Actor/job/application fences still serialize conflicting work; broader deployment load, failover and throughput not certified.

Explain diagnostics run outside transactions on comparable disposable fixtures; actual API uses snapshot transactions. Raw native baseline explain execution may exceed the API query deadline; request outcomes were measured separately.

After measurements, only fixture startup was hardened to explicitly initialize the same schema collections/indexes after connection. Application query code, data/index definitions and five-second budget were unchanged.
performance.provenance: Benchmark pins the original accepted blob recorded in p1.5a-preflight.json, so staging/committing optimized work cannot silently change the baseline.
